brief: Third straight month of higher-than-expected US core inflation (2.8% y/y, three-month annualised near 4%, trending up) combines with Fed governor Waller's hawkish double-hike comment and last Friday's strong jobs report to strengthen SEB's forecast of a December Fed hike. The market now fully prices a 25bp December hike with 15% odds of a double hike, and the US 2-year yield rose about 20bp. US equities fell (S&P 500 down 0.4%, Nasdaq down 0.7%, Nvidia down 5.5%) while European equities rose (Eurostoxx 50 up 0.6%, OMXS30 up 0.5%). Oil is pulled two ways: hopes the Iran war is ending weigh on price, new ship attacks keep a risk premium in place, with Brent near USD 92 a barrel. Abu Dhabi talks between the US, Ukraine and Russia continue a second day. The US called day one productive, but the parties remain far apart on territory and security guarantees. In Norway, October core inflation (CPI-ATE) came in at 2.7%, a tenth below SEB's forecast, supporting SEB's view that inflation will undershoot Norges Bank's expectations. In Sweden, hawkish Riksbank minutes raised officials' inflation risks, but SEB still expects the Riksbank to hold in December and hike once more in March.
